newsitem.title: USA: Memorial canceled for murdered rap singer.
newsitem.headline: Memorial canceled for murdered rap singer.

text.p: A memorial service planned later this week for slain rap singer Tupac Shakur has been cancelled, his record label said Tuesday.

Death Row Records cited "an overwhelming demand for attendance by fans and well-wishers" of Shakur and the "unavailability of a proper venue anywhere in Los Angeles large enough to accommodate the throngs."
A spokesman at the Los Angeles-based "gangsta" rap label said there were no plans for an alternative event and declined further comment.
The cancellation came less than 24 hours after Thursday's memorial at the Wilshire Ebell Theatre near the city's downtown area was announced.
Shakur, 25, died last Friday in Las Vegas, six days after being shot in a gangland-style ambush near the city's famed casinos and hotels.

He was hit four times as he rode with friends to a Las Vegas nightclub after watching the Mike Tyson-Bruce Seldon world heavyweight title fight Saturday night. He had his right lung removed before succumbing to respiratory failure and cardiopulmonary arrest. His family had the body cremated in a private ceremony over the weekend.
No one has been arrested in connection with the shooting, and Las Vegas police have said they have few leads.

One of the most controversial performers of hardcore "gangsta" rap, Shakur sold millions of records whose raw lyrics were laced with violence, sex and profanity. He also received rave notices for his performances in such movies as "Poetic Justice", "Juice" and "Above the Rim".
